key_insight: Choosing a weak-measurement unraveling can substantially reduce average trajectory magic without changing the noisy circuit’s density matrix, but high-magic trajectories persist.
engineering_relevance: Unraveling optimization may lower typical stabilizer-based simulation costs, but average magic alone is insufficient to predict computational savings.
method: Study locally dephased Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits.
Quantify trajectory magic using stabilizer Rényi entropy.
Explore a two-parameter family of minimal Kraus unravelings with state-independent choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a noise-dependent reduction in magic density, while magic remains linear in system size and its trajectory distribution remains broad.
watch_item: A sizable fraction of trajectories retains Haar-random magic and can dominate simulation cost because stabilizer-based costs grow exponentially with magic.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
